title: Hosting Privilege Snapshot and Audit Ingest Guidelines
body:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures a concise, environment-aware mapping of RBAC v2 role families, policy template patterns, SIEM export field contracts, and an evidence automation checklist for quarterly audits and incident investigations. It is intended for security engineers, platform owners, SRE, and compliance partners who operate across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: IAM role layouts and example policy templates; canonical audit export schema for SIEM ingestion; automated evidence bundle patterns; operational runbooks for role changes, onboarding, and audit packaging.
- Audience: sec-eng, platform-eng, product-security reviewers, solutions engineering, SOC engineers.

Context: environment-specific constraints
- Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood-managed control plane): tenant-scoped roles are preferred. Support and platform teams operate under ephemeral least-privilege constructs; network, infra, and customer data access is strictly mediated and recorded. SIEM exports must include tenant_id and request_correlator.
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity in Redwood-managed infra): stronger need for separation of duties between infra-admins and tenant admins; certain privileged operations (node reprovisioning, host-level access) are restricted to Dedicated-Infra role. Evidence collection must include capacity-pool identifiers and physical GPU host metadata when available.
- Private (customer-controlled control plane / on-prem): Redwood provides policy templates and local audit-forwarder hooks. Responsibility for full-chain evidence custody frequently shifts to customer; our templates must enable easy export of signed bundles and clear instructions for KMS/HSM wrapping.

RBAC v2 primitives (quick reference)
- Principal types: human_user, service_account, system_agent (internal runtime), external_integrator (SaaS-to-SaaS identities)
- Role attributes: role_id (stable), version, scope (global | tenant | pool | cluster), bounded_by (timebox|ip_range|justification_ticket), delegatable (bool), audit_label_set (list of strings)
- Policy evaluation: policies evaluate against (principal, action, resource, environment, request_context) and return allow|deny|prompt (requires CA for elevation). All evaluations must be logged with policy_version and decision_trace.

Role family definitions (plain-language)
- Platform-Owner: full lifecycle control over Redwood control plane resources (deploy, upgrade, routing policy). Assigned only in Redwood-managed infra with just-in-time elevation and audit obligations.
- Infra-Operator: node and pool operations (reprovision, reprovision-unsafe, drain); across Dedicated this maps to Dedicated-Infra; in Private this role is split into tenant-only vs operator-with-customer-consent.
- Tenant-Admin: customer-facing admin for model pinning, rollout policies, usage quotas within a tenant scope. No host-level privileges.
- Support-Responder: bounded read and remediate actions for customer incidents; operates with session recording and step-by-step justification that is attached to the audit event.
- Billing-Viewer: read-only access to billing and usage artifacts; cannot read model artifact contents or request payloads.
- Auditor: read-only access to audit logs, evidence bundles, and policy decision traces; cannot impersonate or call privileged actions.
- ServiceAccount-Worker: machine identities used by internal pipelines and customer workloads; should be tenant-scoped where possible and have minimal impersonation capabilities.

Example compact role matrix (human readable)
- Columns: Role Family | Hosted scope | Dedicated scope | Private scope | Typical delegations
- Platform-Owner | global (Redwood) | global/dedicated-owner (Redwood) | N/A or customer-approved | timeboxed, 2-person approval
- Infra-Operator | restricted (no host-level) | pool-scoped (Dedicated hosts) | cluster-scoped with customer approval | audit-labels required
- Tenant-Admin | tenant-scoped | tenant + capacity-pool-assignment | tenant-only | can request service account creation
- Support-Responder | tenant-limited, session-proxy | tenant-limited, with ticket id | tenant-limited | session recorded and tied to incident id
- Auditor | global-read for logs | read-within-contracted-scope | read-only locally | evidence hashes signed, separate key

Policy templates (patterns, not full JSON policy language)
- Allow-with-justification pattern: "Allow [action] on [resource] when principal is in [role_family] AND request_context.justification_ticket exists AND timebox within [start,end]"
- Deny-sensitive-data pattern: "Deny read:model_artifact.content for any principal without role_family Tenant-Admin or Platform-Owner AND request_context.purpose != 'debug'"
- Scoped-imperative pattern for service accounts: "Allow serviceAccount:invoke on models/* for service accounts with label (pipeline=ingest) AND bound_to_tenant = X"
- Impersonation guard: "Allow iam:impersonate for service-account only if impersonator has delegatable=true and ticket_tag contains 'impersonation-approval'"

SIEM export and audit schema (canonical field list)
Provide a minimal contract that SIEM teams can rely on for ingestion and correlation. All fields below are required for Redwood-managed exports; private deployments may map or enrich fields with local metadata.
- event_id: stable UUID for this audit event
- event_ts: RFC3339 timestamp (UTC)
- source: subsystem (iam, authz, serving, pipeline, billing)
- tenant_id: tenant or customer id (nullable for platform-only events)
- principal_id: unique ID for the actor (human or service account)
- principal_type: one of [human_user, service_account, system_agent, external_integrator]
- principal_roles: list of role_ids in effect at time of request
- action: canonical action string (e.g., model.generate, iam.impersonate, node.reprovision)
- resource_type: e.g., model, deployment, pool, node, secret
- resource_id: stable resource identifier
- decision: allow | deny | prompt
- decision_trace: short string or URL to policy decision trace blob (signed)
- policy_version: the policy bundle version evaluated
- request_id: per-request correlator (propagated across services)
- correlation_id: top-level trace id for end-to-end correlation
- client_ip: IP address of request origin
- user_agent: if present
- env_tier: hosted | dedicated | private
- host_metadata: optional object-string (for SIEM use; in dedicated include pool_id, host_id)
- outcome: immediate result (success|failure|partial)
- error_code: optional
- raw_request_snapshot_sha256: hex hash of anonymized request snapshot (if saved)
- evidence_links: list of pre-signed URLs or artifact ids (comma-separated string)

Notes on schema: keep strings short and canonical where possible; include the policy_version and decision_trace link so auditors can perform fast sampling. For Private deployments, require a mapping file that translates local host metadata naming to the canonical fields above.

Evidence automation checklist (for auditors and SRE)
- Daily exports: push compact event batches to SIEM with event_ts within 5s of generation; monitor export latency > 10s as an incident.
- Weekly snapshot: produce signed index of policy bundles deployed across environments (policy_version manifest).
- Quarterly audit bundle: automated job collects the following for the audit window (query range): event batch (gzip), policy bundle manifests, key-rotation statements, ticket references for all allow decisions that required justification, storage-paths for session recordings, and service-account key usage logs. Bundle must be KMS-wrapped and hash-signed.
- Evidence retention: align with customer contract — default Redwood policy is 1 year for full fidelity logs, 3 years for indexed metadata. Private deployments: document the retention contract in onboarding checklist.
- Attestation labels: every elevated session must include an attestation label that is exported as audit_label_set on log events.
- Tamper-evidence: include signed index and manifest; provide verifier script used by auditors to validate signatures and KMS wraps.

Automation patterns and tooling suggestions
- SIEM Ingest Hook: small lambda/forwarder that transforms internal event record to canonical export schema, attaches policy_version, and signs event metadata with a service key. Keep transformation idempotent.
- Evidence-bundler: scheduled job (k8s cronjob) that iterates timeframe windows, pulls events from long-term storage, generates manifest.json, computes SHA256 per-file, and uploads a KMS-wrapped tarball.
- Justification linker: integrate ticketing (JIRA) references into elevation flows; when a role elevation occurs, require either ticket id or recorded session id as a gateway field and surface that in audit logs as justification_ticket.
- Continuous verification: nightly job that samples 100 allow decisions and verifies the evidence_links are reachable and signatures valid. Failure trips a security-channel alert.

Operational playbook: role change and incident scenario
1) Request: Developer or customer requests elevated action (create service account, impersonate, node reprovision). Create a ticket using the standard template that must include reason, timebox, and scope.
2) Approval: Two-person approval for Platform-Owner / Infra-Operator. Approver must attach ticket id; policy engine will accept the elevation only if approval labels are present.
3) Execution: Action is performed via the platform UI/CLI; platform attaches request_id, correlation_id and logs immediate policy decision with decision_trace. Session recording (if interactive) is bound to the event and evidence_links created.
4) Post-change audit: automation picks up the policy_version and event snapshot and adds to weekly snapshot. If the action touches dedicated hardware, bundler adds host_metadata to the bundle.
5) Investigation: SOC pulls the pre-signed evidence bundle, verifies signatures, and cross-checks ticket id + session record.

SIEM-to-alert mapping example (suggestion)
- Alert: "unexpected-impersonation" when action == iam.impersonate AND principal_roles does not include impersonation-allowed role AND decision == allow.
- Alert: "cross-tenant-data-read" when action == data.read AND tenant_id != resource.tenant_id.

SLOs and monitoring for audit exports
- Export latency: 99th percentile < 10s for hosted; 99th < 30s for dedicated; private defines SLA in onboarding.
- Bundle generation: weekly snapshot completion within 6h of window close.
- Evidence availability: pre-signed evidence_links must be available for 30 days after upload for investigation; long-term bundles stored per retention policy.

Open questions and next steps (action items)
- Decide canonical field for "policy_decision_provenance" vs "decision_trace" (compact string or URL to trace?). Action: sec-eng to propose two options and perf test.
- Confirm dedicated host metadata schema (pool_id, rack_id, gpu_serial) — infra to provide sample telemetry.
- Pilot automation in one Dedicated customer and one Hosted tenant to validate policy_version manifest flow.

Appendix: quick example snippets
- Example audit event (flattened CSV-style example line):
event_id=6f8a9c2a-... , event_ts=2024-11-12T19:22:11Z, source=iam, tenant_id=acme-123, principal_id=user:jamal, principal_type=human_user, principal_roles=[support-responder], action=deployment.rollback, resource_type=deployment, resource_id=dep-568, decision=allow, policy_version=v2024-11-05-3, request_id=req-29ab, correlation_id=trace-884, client_ip=35.44.12.2, env_tier=dedicated, evidence_links=gs://evidence-bucket/2024/11/12/bundle-req-29ab.tar.gz

- Example policy template (pseudo-policy english):
"If principal has role support-responder AND justification_ticket is present AND target_deployment.tenant == principal.tenant THEN allow deployment.rollback for that deployment for 60 minutes"

This document is a working artifact — comments welcome. The plan is to iterate into a formal policy JSON library and a small reference implementation of the SIEM export forwarder in the infra repo (github: redwood-infra/audit-forwarder).
